gloss: to rush to; to hurry to the scene

definitions.gloss: to rush to; to hurry to; to come running
definitions.explanation: To hurry to a place upon hearing news, often in response to an emergency, event, or summons.

examples.japanese: {救急車|きゅうきゅうしゃ}がすぐに{駆|か}けつけた。
examples.english: The ambulance rushed to the scene immediately.

examples.japanese: {知|し}らせを{聞|き}いて{病院|びょういん}に{駆|か}けつけた。
examples.english: I rushed to the hospital after hearing the news.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きな{音|おと}がしたので、{近所|きんじょ}の{人|ひと}たちが{次|つぎ}々と{駆|か}けつけてきた。
examples.english: There was a loud noise, so the neighbors came rushing over one after another.

notes:
{駆|か}けつける is an intransitive ichidan verb. A compound of {駆|か}ける (to run/dash) and つける (to arrive at).

ASPECT (ている):
Rarely used in the ている form. The focus is on the act of rushing to a place.

PARTICLE PATTERN:
- [place]に{駆|か}けつける — to rush to [place]

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {現場|げんば}に{駆|か}けつける (rush to the scene)
- {病院|びょういん}に{駆|か}けつける (rush to the hospital)
- {応援|おうえん}に{駆|か}けつける (rush to give support)

Implies urgency and physical movement. Often used when someone responds quickly to an emergency or important event.
